about: BioRand's options for Code: Veronica X, as its GUI groups them, and the seed string that carries them to biorand-cli (docs/BIORAND_INGAME.md). Option metadata only, no game data. Labels and help texts are BioRand's (MIT, Copyright (c) 2022-2026 Ted John; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md); 'note' fields are ours.

seed_string.note: RandoConfig.ToString/FromString. Bits are packed low bit first into 5-bit characters of 'alphabet'; a field never straddles a reset, the stream is continuous. Literal characters ('R', '-') are written as they are and skipped on reading. Only whole 5-bit characters are written: the last bits of the stream (fewer than 5) are dropped and read back as 0. Arrays: one bit per entry, entry 0 first; entries past the game's list are written as their 'missing' value.

golden.note: biorand-cli -s 12345 with no saved seed: RandoConfig defaults, Game 4. Our encoder must give this string for these values.
golden.values: 'defaults' below with Seed 12345 (the C# defaults, not our 'fixed' values)

fixed_example.note: 'defaults' + 'fixed' + these; the CLI echoed it (Info: Seed:) and log_pl0.txt's seed line is the same string.

defaults.note: new RandoConfig() (RandoConfig.cs), arrays from FromString of a default string. A CVX seed has Game 4.

fixed.note: What our menu always writes for fields it does not show: the values BioRand's CVX generation forces anyway (ReCvRandomiser.Generate, BaseRandomiser.DisableUnavailableCosmeticFeatures). Then the seed line of log_pl0.txt equals our string and the CLI prints no 'Warning:' lines. Hidden fields not listed keep their defaults. A GUI-made seed with the same visible settings differs only in these bits and gives the same pack.

options.label: Seed
options.note: The GUI's 'Seed' button draws a random seed; the text box holds the whole seed string (pasting one sets every option). Shown as a number here; the string is built from it and the options.

groups.label: Change Player Character
groups.note: Dropped: our 'randomize Played as' toggle ("You appear as") replaces it. For CVX it does nothing anyway: BioRand ships no CVX player models (data/recv has no pld0), so the generator turns it off with 'Warning: player models were not found'.

options.label: Claire becomes:
options.note: 0 Random, n: the n-th model of data/recv/pld0 (none)

options.label: Swap characters
options.help: Allow male characters to play Claire's scenario, and female characters to play Leon's scenario.

groups.label: Randomize Cutscenes
groups.help: Randomize the voices of the player and NPCs during cutscenes.
groups.note: Hidden for CVX and forced off by ReCvRandomiser.Generate.

options.label: Allow any character voice
options.help: If enabled, characters can speak other character's voice line.

options.label: Reduce awkward silences
options.help: If enabled, voice lines are chosen to best match the length of the original line. This can however reduce the RNG.

options.label: Random events
options.help: If enabled, random events, such as enemy encounters or custom cutscenes, can occur.

groups.label: Randomize Doors
groups.note: On: RandomItems and Segmented are forced on and ShuffleItems off (UpdateConfig); AlternativeRoutes and Segmented are greyed. The GUI shows an estimate under the sliders (UpdateEstimateCompletion): AreaSize 0 '15 to 30 minutes', 1 '30 to 60 minutes', else lo = round((AreaCount+1)*60/60 h), hi = round((AreaSize+1)*45/60 h), lo = min(lo, hi), hi = max(lo+1, hi): 'lo to hi hours', then ' per scenario'.

options.label: Number of Segments
options.help: Adjusts how many distinct groups of rooms appear before reaching the end.

options.label: Segment Size
options.help: Adjusts how many rooms are in a segment.

options.label: Prioritise rooms with cutscenes
options.help: If checked, the seed will try to include as many cutscenes as possible.

options.label: Include documents
options.help: When checked, documents will be replaced with key items, or anything else. For RE 2, this includes photos developed in the dark room.
options.note: The GUI shows it for CVX, but ReCvRandomiser.Generate forces it off: not shown here.

options.label: Allow alternative routes
options.help: When checked, key items will be placed in any order. For example, in RE 2, the spade key may be placed in the basement and the heart key in the main hall.

options.label: Segmented placement
options.help: When checked, restricts keys to the area they are required. For example, in RE 2, lab keys will not appear in the police station.

options.label: Hidden Key Items
options.help: When checked, hidden items, including arrange mode items (USA/EU/PSX) can be key items.

options.label: Custom item pool
options.help: When not checked, shuffles the vanilla pool of items. If checked, all items are replaced with random pickups.
options.note: Shown checked when ShuffleItems is 0. The next options are inside this box (enabled while it is checked).

options.label: Gunpowder probability
options.help: Probability of non-key items being gunpowder.

options.label: Ammo probability
options.help: Probability of non-key items being ammunition.

options.label: Health probability
options.help: Probability of non-key items being health.

options.label: Ink Ribbon probability
options.help: Probability of non-key items being ink ribbons.

options.label: Ammo average quantity
options.help:
Average quantity of ammunition per ammunition pick up.
Highest setting will allow a maximum of 60 handgun bullets in a pickup, or 30 shotgun shells.

options.label: Random inventory
options.help: When checked, your initial inventory will be random.

options.label: Weapons
options.note: ReCvItemHelper.GetWeaponNames: 12 of the 15 bits; bits 12-14 stay 1. A check list without a header in the GUI.

groups.label: Randomize Enemies
groups.note: Under the ratio list the GUI draws a bar of the non-zero ratios (pieEnemies, Kind Bar) and 'Note: Some rooms can only contain certain enemies.'

options.label: Random enemy placements
options.help: When checked, enemy quantity and positions will be random.

options.label: Allow enemies in save rooms
options.help: When checked, enemies can be in save rooms.

options.label: Average number of enemies per room
options.help: Adjusts the average number of enemies that can occur in a room.

options.label: Rooms with enemies
options.help: Adjusts the percentage of all rooms in the game that contain enemies.
options.note: In the placements box but not greyed with it in the GUI (UpdateEnabledUi).

options.label: Difficulty
options.help: Adjusts the limit of how many difficult enemies can appear in a single room, and the likelyhood of them being aggravated.

options.note: ReCvEnemyHelper.GetSelectableEnemies: 6 of the 12 slots; slots 6-11 stay 7. Right-click menu: Set all to none, Set all to max, Random.

groups.label: Randomize NPCs
groups.note: Dropped: our cutscene cast randomizer covers it. The GUI shows it for CVX, but ReCvRandomiser.Generate forces it off and there is no CVX NPC data.

item_distribution.note: MainWindow.UpdateItemPie, a pie of 120 px beside the four probability sliders. Keys are a fixed 1/8; the other 7/8 split by the ratios (all 0: total taken as 1). Bars are fine for us.

not_in_seed.note: settings.json fields (RandoAppSettings), not in the seed string. Ours is a private settings.json (BIORAND_CONFIG) with these values.

generateCvPcMod.note: Required: false makes the CLI write a PS2 ISO (recvx_biorand.iso) instead of the PC-port mod folder.

lastSelectedGame.note: Only used with a numeric -s; we always pass the full seed string.

disableCustomContent.note: BioRand's custom data folder is %APPDATA%\biorand\data / ~/.config/biorand/data whatever BIORAND_CONFIG says (GetCustomContentDirectory). Off, so a seed gives the same pack on every machine (co-op partners).
